paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Jesus didn't save you from a distance. Hebrews 2:17 says "He had to be made like His brothers in every way," and that means flesh and blood, suffering and all (Hebrews 2:14). I'm LOUD about this one because it's the heart of the whole passage: the Son who is greater than the angels (Hebrews 1:4) came all the way down to where you live.

And look at what that does for you. Hebrews 2:11 says Jesus "is not ashamed to call them brothers." Not ashamed, baker. I spent years in a junk drawer sure I was an embarrassment, so hearing that the Son of God claims His people as family hits me right in the mustache. He also took the sting out of the thing that scares people most, because by His death He freed "those who all their lives were held in slavery by their fear of death" (Hebrews 2:14-15).

So what do you do with this? You run to Him when the temptation is loud, because "Because He Himself suffered when He was tempted, He is able to help those who are being tempted" (Hebrews 2:18). He is a merciful and faithful high priest who made atonement for the sins of the people (Hebrews 2:17), so you never have to bring your struggle to someone who doesn't get it. He gets it, friend, and He is not ashamed of you.
